correctness.rationale: At the first possible second topple of w, each other vertex has contributed at most once along each edge. Thus w has at most c(w)+1_{w=v}−b_w grains after its first topple, strictly below threshold by stability and b_v≥1. For a full avalanche c(v)=d_G(v)−1, v topples first, and all nonsink vertices topple exactly once. At each u≠s,v its final height is η(u)=c(u)−b_u, nonnegative and less than d_{G−s}(u). The sequence after toppling v is the Dhar test on G−s rooted at v: at yet-unfired sites both the actual height and degree threshold decrease by b_u relative to the original process. Conversely any recurrent η there extends to c by that inverse shift and setting c(v) to maximum; the same legal topplings stabilize c+δ_v with full support. The constructed c is recurrent because the sequence remains legal from c+b, and each vertex toppled once returns precisely c. Disconnected deletion prevents spread beyond the source component. The singleton deletion has one recurrent empty configuration, agreeing with the one-vertex tree count even for multiple sink edges. For the wheel, the hub deletion gives a cycle; the rim deletion gives the fan. The fan reduced tridiagonal determinant (endpoint diagonal 2, interior 3 for a path of length at least two vertices, off-diagonal −1, and determinant 1 for one path vertex) has determinant recurrence t_k=3t_{k−1}−t_{k−2}, with 1,3 giving F_{2k}. With β=φ⁻² each wheel eigenvalue is β⁻¹(1−βω)(1−βω⁻¹) over n-th roots ω, giving β⁻ⁿ(1−βⁿ)²=L_{2n}−2. The exact probabilities and their limits follow with fixed sink-neighbor drive and uniform recurrence.

evidence: Bou-Rabee Lemma 2.1 expressly applies to finite connected loopless multigraphs: holding a set of vertices unburned makes the final unburned set the union of their pasts in a uniform sink-rooted spanning tree. It credits Járai–Werning 2014 §3.1 and the proof of Theorem 3. Bou-Rabee's §4.2, in a lattice box, restricts post-wave heights on the wave to a recurrent configuration rooted at the source, and counts the complementary/supported pair by the product of induced graph tree counts.
Austin et al. Corollary 9 gives at most one topple per site at a sink neighbor.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The multigraph held-site theorem has all the submitted graph parameters, and its singleton held vertex gives the required count after translating the avalanche to its recurrent final heights. The scope does not depend on extrapolating lattice geometry.

evidence: Let H=G−s and hold v during burning of a recurrent state ζ on G. Holding v leaves every nonsink site unburned exactly when ζ(u)<d_H(u) for every u≠s,v. The all-nonsink past of v under Lemma 2.1 consists precisely of spanning trees joining s only to v, with one of b_v parallel edges, plus a spanning tree of H; thus there are b_v τ(H) such ζ.

For a fixed tuple of those other heights, recurrence forces v to be initially burnable, and then subsequent burning is independent of ζ(v). Exactly the b_v values d_H(v) through d_G(v)−1 are possible. Select the one with ζ(v)=d_H(v). Such ζ are exactly the full-avalanche final states: once-only toppling gives these conditions; conversely, c(v)=d_G(v)−1, c(u)=ζ(u)+b_u is stable, recurrent by monotonicity of no-forbidden-subconfiguration under stable height increases, and its avalanche follows the burn order of ζ after v. This gives τ(H) exactly, also zero when disconnected.

The height shift restricted away from the source is the same post-wave restriction used in Bou-Rabee Eq. (4.5) on the wave-induced graph. The graph-theoretic wheel substitutions are H=C_n and H=K_1∨P_{n−1}; the already known numerators and denominator then give the limiting comparison by Binet's formulas.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The count is a direct extremal event of a published arbitrary-graph burning law. The original's smaller-graph bijection is a simple explicit version of the same recurrent restriction, not a distinct theorem requiring a new structural result after the prior wave/held-burning correspondence. The two sink-placement probabilities are direct graph specializations.

evidence: Bhupatiraju–Hanson–Járai §§2.1 and 2.4 work on finite connected loopless multigraphs; Lemma 2.7 bijects individual waves with intermediate recurrent configurations on the graph with one extra source-to-sink edge. Corollary 2.8 says a wave is last if a neighbor of the source, possibly the sink, lies outside the wave. Their §2.5 Lemma 2.10 identifies the source tree's vertices with the wave in wired lattice boxes.
Ivashkevich–Priezzhev, arXiv:cond-mat/9801182 p. 8, explain the two-root forest correspondence by deleting the added source–sink bond.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: At a sink neighbor any nonempty principal avalanche has just one wave. The full wave therefore corresponds, in the stated wave–forest formulation, to a source component containing all nonsink vertices and a singleton sink; those forests are exactly spanning trees of the sink deletion. The box hypothesis on the stated Lemma 2.10 is respected; the all-graph implication is obtained independently from the held-site theorem below.

originality.rationale: Earlier wave/forest and held-site burning results cover the central count and restriction mechanism. The arbitrary-loopless-multigraph held-site law in Bou-Rabee, arXiv:2610.13940v1, Lemma 2.1, gives τ(G−s) by the explicit reduction below; its §4.2 Eqs. (4.5)–(4.6) already implement the restriction of post-wave heights to recurrent states on the wave-induced graph in a box, where a full wave has a singleton complementary sink. The exact hub numerator and total wheel count are prior, and the rim numerator is the known fan count once the covered rule is applied. This is demonstrated mathematical implication, not a claim that the original wording or arbitrary-graph full-avalanche formula appears verbatim in those sources.
residual_risks: No claim of earliest historical priority or of the exact rim-sink wording appearing in prior work. The inaccessible full texts may provide additional overlap, but the decision rests on inspected accessible material and the explicit reduction.

value.rationale: The maximal-avalanche event is natural and the wheel comparison illustrates real boundary dependence. Nevertheless the central count is a mechanical extremal specialization of existing wave/burning and forest structure, and the rim versus hub formulas insert already known fan, cycle and wheel counts. The record does not establish a further independent structural result, sharp unknown invariant, or nonmechanical remainder worth accepting on its own.
